faq.q: How much does Law Offices of Robert E. Brown charge?
faq.a: Law Offices of Robert E. Brown publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Law Offices of Robert E. Brown offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Law Offices of Robert E. Brown publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock.

faq.q: Where does Law Offices of Robert E. Brown have offices?
faq.a: Law Offices of Robert E. Brown publishes two offices, in Manhattan and Staten Island. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Law Offices of Robert E. Brown?
faq.a: Law Offices of Robert E. Brown names no attorney on the public pages we could read. That is a gap in what the firm publishes rather than a statement about who works there, and it is why the licensure and discipline checks on this profile have nothing to run against.

faq.q: What has Law Firm Listings verified about Law Offices of Robert E. Brown?
faq.a: Law Offices of Robert E. Brown scores 39 and sits at Listed. Passed: entity registration and footprint. Did not pass: website. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure and discipline.
